questions.question: What is the correct definition of cloud computing?

options.text: Buying and owning servers in your office
On-demand delivery of IT resources with pay-as-you-go pricing
Renting a physical data center from a third party
Storing files on a USB drive connected to the internet

explanation.correct: Cloud computing is the on-demand delivery of compute power, storage, databases, and other IT resources through a cloud service platform with pay-as-you-go pricing.
explanation.why: A is on-premises IT. C is colocation, not cloud. D describes local storage, not cloud.

questions.question: Which keyword best describes the pricing model of cloud computing?

options.text: Subscription-only
Upfront payment
Pay-as-you-go
Annual commitment required

explanation.correct: Cloud computing uses pay-as-you-go pricing — you pay only for what you use, when you use it, and stop paying when you stop using it.
explanation.why: Upfront payment describes CAPEX (on-premises). Subscription and annual commitment describe some pricing models but not the core cloud definition.

questions.question: Which component of a server handles mathematical computations and processing?

options.text: RAM
Storage
CPU
Router

explanation.correct: The CPU (Central Processing Unit) handles computations and processing logic.
explanation.why: RAM is short-term memory for fast data access. Storage is long-term data retention. A router is a networking device.

questions.question: What is a Router in traditional networking?

options.text: A device that stores data permanently
A device that forwards data packets between networks
A device that assigns IP addresses to servers
A device that encrypts network traffic

explanation.correct: A router forwards data packets between networks and knows where to send packets on the internet — like a postal sorting hub.
explanation.why: A is storage. C is a DHCP server function. D is a firewall/VPN function.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the five NIST characteristics of cloud computing?

options.text: On-demand self-service
Rapid elasticity
Dedicated hardware for each customer
Measured service

explanation.correct: Dedicated hardware for each customer is NOT a cloud characteristic — it describes traditional IT. Cloud uses multi-tenancy (resource pooling), where multiple customers share physical infrastructure.
explanation.why: On-demand self-service, rapid elasticity, and measured service are all NIST cloud characteristics. Resource pooling (shared, not dedicated) is the correct fifth characteristic.

questions.question: What does 'resource pooling' mean in cloud computing?

options.text: Each customer gets their own dedicated physical server
Multiple customers share the same physical infrastructure with logical isolation
Resources are pooled by geography only
AWS pools unused resources and deletes them

explanation.correct: Resource pooling (multi-tenancy) means multiple AWS customers share the same physical infrastructure while being logically isolated from each other.
explanation.why: A describes dedicated hosting, not cloud. C and D are incorrect interpretations.

questions.question: In cloud computing terminology, what is the difference between CAPEX and OPEX?

options.text: CAPEX is monthly billing; OPEX is annual billing
CAPEX is upfront hardware investment; OPEX is ongoing operational spending
CAPEX applies to SaaS; OPEX applies to IaaS
CAPEX is AWS's cost; OPEX is the customer's cost

explanation.correct: CAPEX (capital expenditure) is upfront spending on assets like servers. OPEX (operational expenditure) is ongoing pay-as-you-use spending. Cloud shifts spending from CAPEX to OPEX.
explanation.why: Billing frequency alone doesn't define the distinction. CAPEX vs OPEX is a financial accounting concept tied to ownership vs consumption.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a SaaS (Software as a Service) product?

options.text: Amazon EC2
AWS Elastic Beanstalk
Gmail
AWS VPC

explanation.correct: Gmail is a complete software product run and managed by Google — users just use the email application without managing any infrastructure.
explanation.why: EC2 is IaaS. Elastic Beanstalk is PaaS. VPC is an AWS networking service (IaaS level).

questions.question: What is an AWS Region?

options.text: A single data center run by AWS
A group of Edge Locations in a geographic area
A physical geographic location containing a cluster of data centers
A logical grouping of AWS accounts

explanation.correct: An AWS Region is a physical geographic location in the world that contains a cluster of AWS data centers (organized into Availability Zones).
explanation.why: A single data center is an AZ component, not a Region. Edge Locations are separate from Regions. Regions are geographic, not account-based.

questions.question: What is the MINIMUM number of Availability Zones in every AWS Region?

explanation.correct: Every AWS Region has a minimum of 3 Availability Zones. The maximum is 6. The typical number is 3.
explanation.why: 1 and 2 AZs would not provide adequate fault isolation. 6 is the maximum, not the minimum.

questions.question: Which AWS service is classified as a GLOBAL service (not region-specific)?

options.text: Amazon EC2
Amazon RDS
AWS IAM
AWS Lambda

explanation.correct: AWS IAM (Identity and Access Management) is a global service — IAM users, roles, and policies apply across all regions, with no region selection required.
explanation.why: EC2, RDS, and Lambda are all regional services — they must be created within a specific AWS region.

questions.question: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, which of the following is AWS's responsibility?

options.text: Configuring security groups on EC2 instances
Encrypting data stored in S3
Physical security of data centers
Patching the OS on EC2 instances

explanation.correct: Physical security of AWS data centers is AWS's responsibility — this includes building access controls, cameras, and guards. Customers have no control over or access to this.
explanation.why: Security groups, S3 encryption, and EC2 OS patching are all customer responsibilities under the Shared Responsibility Model.

questions.question: A company wants to deploy an application in the cloud but must keep all customer data within their country due to regulatory requirements. Which factor should be the PRIMARY consideration when selecting an AWS Region?

options.text: Pricing — choose the cheapest region
Latency — choose the nearest region
Compliance — ensure data sovereignty requirements are met
Service availability — ensure all required services are present

explanation.correct: Compliance (data sovereignty) is the primary factor — legal requirements override all other considerations. If law requires data to stay in a country, you must deploy in that region regardless of cost or latency.
explanation.why: Pricing, latency, and service availability are important but secondary. Compliance is non-negotiable and always takes priority.

questions.question: A startup experiences 10x traffic spikes every Friday evening compared to weekday mornings. Which cloud characteristic BEST solves their capacity planning problem?

options.text: Broad network access — users can connect from anywhere
Rapid elasticity — automatically scale resources based on demand
Measured service — pay only for what you use
Resource pooling — share physical infrastructure with others

explanation.correct: Rapid elasticity allows resources to scale up during peak demand (Friday spike) and scale back down during off-peak times (weekday morning) automatically — solving the capacity mismatch problem.
explanation.why: Broad network access is about connectivity, not capacity. Measured service is about billing. Resource pooling is about multi-tenancy.

questions.question: A developer pushes code to their platform and the underlying OS, runtime, and scaling infrastructure are all automatically managed. Which cloud service model is being used?

options.text: IaaS — the developer manages the OS
PaaS — the developer only manages application and data
SaaS — everything is managed by the provider
On-premises — the company manages everything

explanation.correct: PaaS (Platform as a Service) removes the need to manage infrastructure. The developer focuses only on deploying and managing their application and data — the platform handles OS, runtime, patching, and scaling.
explanation.why: IaaS requires the customer to manage the OS. SaaS means the customer doesn't even manage the application. The scenario describes code deployment without OS concerns — that's PaaS.

questions.question: An e-commerce company notices that running servers 24/7 costs the same whether they have 1 visitor or 1 million visitors. After migrating to AWS, their bill drops 60% because they now scale down at night. Which cloud advantage did they realize?

options.text: Increased speed and agility
Economies of scale
Stop guessing capacity — pay only for actual usage
Go global in minutes

explanation.correct: By moving from fixed-capacity on-premises servers to elastic cloud resources, the company now pays for actual usage. Scaling down at night means paying for less — directly solving the capacity guessing problem.
explanation.why: Speed and agility is about development velocity. Economies of scale is about AWS's purchasing power reducing prices. Go global is about geographic expansion.

questions.question: Under the Shared Responsibility Model, a company runs MySQL on Amazon EC2. Who is responsible for patching the MySQL database engine?

options.text: AWS — they manage all database software
The customer — they manage the OS and all software on EC2
Shared — AWS patches the engine; customer patches the OS
The AWS RDS team — they manage all relational databases

explanation.correct: When MySQL runs on EC2 (IaaS), the customer manages everything above the hypervisor — including the OS, MySQL installation, and MySQL patching. AWS only manages the physical hardware and hypervisor.
explanation.why: AWS manages MySQL patching only when using Amazon RDS (a managed service). On EC2, the customer is fully responsible for any software they install.

questions.question: Which deployment model would BEST suit a financial company that must keep trading data on-premises for regulatory reasons but wants cloud-based analytics for non-sensitive marketing data?

options.text: Private Cloud — keep everything internal
Public Cloud — migrate everything to AWS
Hybrid Cloud — keep sensitive data on-premises, use AWS for analytics
Multi-Cloud — use two different public clouds

explanation.correct: Hybrid Cloud mixes on-premises infrastructure with public cloud. The company keeps regulated trading data on-premises while using AWS for flexible, scalable analytics workloads — the ideal balance.
explanation.why: Private cloud doesn't provide the cloud benefits needed. Full public cloud migration would violate regulations. Multi-cloud doesn't specifically solve the on-premises requirement.

questions.question: A team in Mumbai is accessing an application hosted in the AWS us-east-1 (Northern Virginia) region. Users complain of high latency. What is the MOST appropriate solution?

options.text: Upgrade to a larger EC2 instance type in us-east-1
Enable Multi-AZ deployment in us-east-1
Deploy the application in the ap-south-1 (Mumbai) region
Use a private cloud deployment model

explanation.correct: Latency is caused by geographic distance. Deploying in the Mumbai region (ap-south-1) moves the application closer to users in India, dramatically reducing round-trip network time.
explanation.why: Larger EC2 instances improve compute performance, not network latency. Multi-AZ improves availability, not latency for distant users. Private cloud doesn't solve geographic latency.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between an AWS Region and Availability Zones?

options.text: An Availability Zone contains multiple Regions
A Region contains multiple Availability Zones
Regions and Availability Zones are the same thing
Edge Locations are inside Availability Zones

explanation.correct: A Region is a geographic area that contains multiple Availability Zones (typically 3). Each AZ consists of one or more isolated data centers.
explanation.why: The hierarchy is: Region → Availability Zones → Data Centers. Edge Locations are separate from this hierarchy.

questions.question: A company currently spends $500,000/year on server hardware that they use at only 30% capacity on average. Moving to AWS would allow them to pay only for 30% capacity. Which economic benefit does this represent?

options.text: Economies of scale
Going global in minutes
Trading CAPEX for OPEX and eliminating wasted capacity
Increased agility

explanation.correct: This represents two combined benefits: trading CAPEX (upfront hardware purchase) for OPEX (usage-based), and stopping capacity guessing — now they only pay for what they use (30%), eliminating 70% waste.
explanation.why: Economies of scale refers to AWS's own bulk purchasing reducing prices. Going global is about geography. Agility is about development speed.

questions.question: Which AWS infrastructure component is designed to serve content to end users with the LOWEST possible latency by caching content close to them?

options.text: Availability Zones
AWS Regions
Edge Locations / Points of Presence
VPC Subnets

explanation.correct: Edge Locations (Points of Presence) are distributed globally across 400+ locations and are used by services like CloudFront to cache and serve content close to end users, minimizing latency.
explanation.why: AZs provide fault isolation within a region, not content delivery optimization. Regions are large geographic clusters. VPC subnets are network segmentation within a region.

questions.question: Which of the following is the customer's responsibility under the Shared Responsibility Model for Amazon RDS?

options.text: Patching the underlying database engine
Managing the physical servers hosting the database
Configuring database users and access permissions
Patching the operating system running RDS

explanation.correct: For RDS (a managed PaaS service), AWS handles OS patching, database engine patching, and hardware management. The customer is responsible for database-level configuration — including users, access permissions, encryption settings, and what data they store.
explanation.why: Database engine patching and OS patching are AWS's responsibility for managed services like RDS. Physical server management is always AWS's responsibility.

questions.question: Data transfer pricing in AWS follows a specific pattern. Which statement is CORRECT?

options.text: Data IN and data OUT are both charged at the same rate
Data IN to AWS is free; data OUT from AWS to the internet is charged
Data OUT to AWS is free; data IN from AWS is charged
All data transfer within the same region is always charged

explanation.correct: AWS charges for data transfer OUT to the internet but does not charge for data transfer IN. This asymmetric pricing model incentivizes migrating data to AWS (free ingress) while the egress cost is the usage charge.
explanation.why: Data OUT being charged is the correct rule. Data IN is always free. Intra-region data transfer pricing varies by service but is generally low.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST explains why prices for AWS services have generally decreased over time?

options.text: AWS reduces prices to match competitors' pricing
AWS benefits from economies of scale as millions of customers share infrastructure costs
AWS reduces prices because servers become obsolete quickly
AWS offers discounts as a marketing strategy to attract new customers

explanation.correct: As AWS grows and millions of customers share the same global infrastructure, AWS can operate more efficiently and at lower cost per unit. These savings are passed on to customers — this is the economies of scale advantage.
explanation.why: While competition influences pricing, the core mechanism is operational efficiency from massive scale. Server obsolescence affects costs but is not the primary driver.

questions.question: A company is evaluating whether to use AWS Elastic Beanstalk or Amazon EC2 to host their web application. The team wants to focus entirely on writing code and not manage OS updates, server provisioning, or load balancer configuration. Which should they choose and why?

options.text: Amazon EC2 — it gives more control over the environment
AWS Elastic Beanstalk — it abstracts infrastructure management, letting the team focus on code
Amazon EC2 — it supports more programming languages
AWS Elastic Beanstalk — it's cheaper than EC2 for all workloads

explanation.correct: Elastic Beanstalk is PaaS — it handles provisioning, load balancing, auto-scaling, and OS management automatically. The team simply deploys code. This directly solves their stated need.
explanation.why: EC2 (IaaS) requires the team to manage OS, provisioning, and load balancers themselves — the opposite of what they want. Cost comparison is workload-dependent, not always in Beanstalk's favor.

questions.question: An AWS customer's EC2 instance was compromised because they forgot to change the default SSH port. Which party failed in their responsibility?

options.text: AWS — they should have enforced port changes
The customer — configuring network and security settings is their responsibility
AWS — they should have monitored for compromise
Shared equally between AWS and the customer

explanation.correct: Security configuration of EC2 instances — including security groups, firewall rules, and network configuration — is the customer's responsibility. AWS is not responsible for how customers configure their resources.
explanation.why: AWS manages the physical infrastructure and hypervisor. Everything above that, including OS and network configuration, is the customer's domain.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the six advantages of cloud computing defined by AWS?

options.text: Trade capital expense for operational expense
Benefit from massive economies of scale
Eliminate the need for an internet connection
Stop guessing capacity

explanation.correct: Eliminating the need for an internet connection is NOT a cloud advantage — in fact, cloud computing requires broad network access (internet connectivity). All other options are legitimate AWS-defined advantages.
explanation.why: All of the other three are genuine advantages. Broad network access (requiring internet) is actually one of the five NIST characteristics of cloud computing.

questions.question: A company's application runs on 50 servers. At 3 AM, only 5 servers are needed. By 9 AM, they need all 50. With traditional on-premises IT, they still pay for all 50 servers at 3 AM. Which cloud advantage directly solves this?

options.text: Go global in minutes
Stop guessing capacity — scale in and out automatically
Benefit from massive economies of scale
Increase speed and agility

explanation.correct: Rapid elasticity (the ability to stop guessing capacity) means the company can scale down to 5 servers at 3 AM and scale back up to 50 at 9 AM, paying only for active resources at each point.
explanation.why: Going global is about geography. Economies of scale is about AWS's bulk pricing. Speed and agility is about development velocity.

questions.question: Which statement CORRECTLY distinguishes between a Private Cloud and a Public Cloud?

options.text: Private clouds have lower latency than public clouds
Private clouds are used by a single organization and are not exposed to the public; public clouds are shared by many customers
Private clouds use pay-as-you-go pricing; public clouds require upfront payment
Private clouds are hosted on-premises only; public clouds are hosted abroad

explanation.correct: Private clouds are used exclusively by one organization and not exposed to the general public. Public clouds like AWS are operated by third-party providers and resources are shared (with logical isolation) among many customers.
explanation.why: Latency depends on proximity, not cloud type. Private clouds often have higher costs, not lower. Private clouds can be hosted by third parties (like Rackspace).

questions.question: A multinational company wants to deploy a web application. Their primary users are in Germany. German data protection law requires user data to stay within Germany. However, they also need a service called Amazon Kinesis which is NOT available in the Frankfurt region. What should they do?

options.text: Deploy in us-east-1 (cheapest) and ignore the compliance requirement
Deploy user data processing in eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) and use Kinesis in another region for non-PII data
Use an on-premises solution since cloud can't meet the requirement
Deploy entirely in eu-west-1 (Ireland) since it's the nearest available region

explanation.correct: This is a multi-constraint problem. Compliance requires user (PII) data in Frankfurt. Non-PII data can use Kinesis in another region. A hybrid-region architecture satisfies both compliance and service availability constraints.
explanation.why: Ignoring compliance violates the law. Full on-premises is unnecessary — cloud architecture can accommodate. Deploying to Ireland moves PII outside Germany, violating the data residency requirement.

questions.question: A company currently has 1 million active users and uses AWS with auto-scaling. Their competitor suddenly shuts down, and they expect to gain 5 million new users over the next 48 hours. Which cloud characteristic makes this scenario survivable WITHOUT pre-planning?

options.text: Measured service — they'll get an accurate bill
Broad network access — users can connect from anywhere
Rapid elasticity — resources scale out automatically to meet demand spikes
On-demand self-service — engineers can manually provision more servers

explanation.correct: Rapid elasticity enables automatic scaling without manual intervention. The auto-scaling group expands capacity to handle 6x the normal load without requiring advance hardware purchases or manual provisioning.
explanation.why: Measured service is about billing. Broad network access is about connectivity. On-demand self-service is about provisioning ability, but rapid elasticity specifically addresses automatic scaling without human intervention.

questions.question: Under the Shared Responsibility Model, which scenario represents a SHARED responsibility between AWS and the customer?

options.text: Physical destruction of a failed hard drive in an AWS data center
Applying patches to an Amazon EC2 operating system
Encrypting data in Amazon S3 using server-side encryption
Patch management and configuration management for EC2 and managed services combined

explanation.correct: Patch management is shared: for EC2 (IaaS), the customer patches the OS; for managed services like RDS, AWS patches the database engine. This means overall patch management responsibility is split — making it truly shared.
explanation.why: Physical hard drive destruction is always AWS. EC2 OS patching is always the customer. S3 encryption enabling is the customer's choice. The patch management split across service types is the correct 'shared' example.

questions.question: A solutions architect must choose between deploying an application in eu-west-1 (Ireland) or eu-central-1 (Frankfurt). The application needs to comply with GDPR, the users are primarily in Germany, and eu-central-1 is 30% more expensive. What is the CORRECT order of decision factors?

options.text: Price → Latency → Compliance → Service Availability
Compliance → Latency → Service Availability → Price
Latency → Compliance → Price → Service Availability
Service Availability → Price → Compliance → Latency

explanation.correct: Compliance is non-negotiable and comes first. If GDPR requires data to stay within a jurisdiction, that overrides cost. Then latency (proximity to German users favors Frankfurt). Then service availability. Pricing is the last tiebreaker.
explanation.why: Price is important but legal compliance is non-negotiable. Latency affects user experience but doesn't override law. The correct AWS priority order starts with compliance.

questions.question: A company runs a web application on EC2. The security team finds that someone exploited a vulnerability in the Apache web server the company installed. Which party is responsible, and why?

options.text: AWS — they should have prevented the vulnerability
AWS — they manage all software on EC2 instances
The customer — they installed and are responsible for all software on their EC2 instances
Shared — AWS manages the server, customer manages the application

explanation.correct: Under the Shared Responsibility Model, the customer is responsible for all software they install on EC2 (IaaS), including web servers like Apache. Patching Apache, configuring it securely, and monitoring for vulnerabilities is entirely the customer's job.
explanation.why: AWS manages the hypervisor and physical hardware. They do not manage applications customers install on their EC2 instances. The 'shared' model doesn't mean equal split — boundaries are precise.

questions.question: Which combination of AWS infrastructure elements provides the HIGHEST level of fault tolerance for an application?

options.text: Multiple EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone
Multiple EC2 instances spread across multiple Availability Zones in the same Region
Multiple EC2 instances in the same Region but with large instance types
Multiple RDS read replicas in the same Availability Zone

explanation.correct: Spreading instances across multiple AZs ensures that if one AZ experiences a failure (power outage, network failure, disaster), the application continues running in other AZs. This is the architectural basis for high availability on AWS.
explanation.why: Multiple instances in the same AZ share the same failure domain. Larger instances don't improve fault tolerance — they're a single point of failure. Read replicas in the same AZ share the same failure risk.

questions.question: Which statement about AWS Availability Zones is MOST accurate?

options.text: AZs are connected with high-bandwidth, ultra-low latency private networking and are physically separated to provide disaster isolation
AZs are identical to Regions but used for redundancy
AZs are always exactly one data center each
AZs in different regions can be directly connected for cross-region replication

explanation.correct: AZs are physically separated from each other to ensure disasters don't cascade between them, yet they're connected with high-bandwidth private networking for low-latency data replication. This combination makes them the foundation of high availability architecture.
explanation.why: AZs exist within a single Region, not across regions. AZs may contain one or more data centers (AWS doesn't specify). Cross-region connections exist but AZs are region-specific.

questions.question: A startup is planning to build a real-time recommendation engine using a third-party ML service via API. They only need to send data and receive predictions — they don't manage any servers or models. Which cloud service model does this represent?

options.text: IaaS — they have access to compute resources
PaaS — they're using a platform to build their application
SaaS — they're consuming a complete, managed service via API
On-premises — they have full control of the model

explanation.correct: When you consume a complete service via API without managing any infrastructure, runtime, or models — that's SaaS. Amazon Rekognition works this way: send an image, get predictions. No servers, no models to train.
explanation.why: IaaS provides raw compute. PaaS provides a development platform. SaaS provides ready-to-use software services — including ML APIs where all model management is hidden from the customer.

questions.question: An enterprise company argues that moving to public cloud increases their security risk because multiple companies share the same physical infrastructure. A cloud architect disagrees. Which response BEST defends the cloud architecture?

options.text: Physical separation still exists even in public cloud
Multi-tenancy uses strong logical isolation at the hypervisor level, and AWS's physical security exceeds what most enterprises can implement themselves
The risk is real, so enterprises should only use private cloud
Multi-tenancy doesn't exist in AWS — each customer gets dedicated hardware by default

explanation.correct: Multi-tenancy uses hypervisor-level isolation that prevents customers from accessing each other's data. Additionally, AWS's physical data center security (biometrics, armed guards, 24/7 surveillance) typically exceeds what enterprises implement themselves.
explanation.why: Physical separation doesn't exist in the same way — shared hardware is the cloud model. Recommending private cloud-only dismisses valid public cloud use. AWS does offer Dedicated Hosts but shared is the default.

questions.question: AWS has over 400 Points of Presence globally. What PRIMARY purpose do they serve?

options.text: They serve as backup data centers for AWS Regions
They provide additional EC2 compute capacity near major cities
They cache and deliver content to end users with the lowest possible latency via CloudFront
They serve as the connection points between AWS Regions

explanation.correct: Points of Presence (Edge Locations) are primarily used by Amazon CloudFront (CDN) to cache content — videos, images, static files — close to end users. When a user requests content, it's served from the nearest PoP rather than a distant Region.
explanation.why: Regions contain full data centers, not PoPs. EC2 runs in Regions/AZs, not Edge Locations. Region interconnection happens via AWS's private backbone network, not Edge Locations.

questions.question: Which of the following scenarios would MOST benefit from a Hybrid Cloud deployment model?

options.text: A brand-new startup with no existing infrastructure launching a mobile app
A bank that must keep transaction records on-premises due to regulation, but wants cloud for fraud analytics
A content streaming company that wants to expand to a new country
A small business replacing their email server with Gmail

explanation.correct: A bank with regulatory requirements for on-premises data storage that also wants cloud capabilities for analytics is the textbook hybrid cloud use case — combining on-premises infrastructure with public cloud services.
explanation.why: A new startup has no legacy infrastructure — fully public cloud makes more sense. Content expansion is a public cloud geography scenario. Replacing email with Gmail is pure SaaS/public cloud.

questions.question: What is the significance of AWS launching in 2004 with SQS as its first public service?

options.text: It shows AWS started as a messaging company
It demonstrates that AWS's internal infrastructure was strong enough to offer as a service to others
It proves that SQS is the most important AWS service
It shows AWS was always intended to be a public service from day one

explanation.correct: AWS grew from Amazon's need to manage its own massive e-commerce infrastructure. When they realized the internal IT could be externalized, they started offering it publicly — beginning with SQS in 2004.
explanation.why: AWS began as an e-commerce company's IT infrastructure, not a messaging company. SQS's historical primacy doesn't make it architecturally most important. AWS was not originally designed to be public.

questions.question: Which statement about AWS pricing for networking is CORRECT?

options.text: All data transfer in AWS is free, including between regions
Data transfer into AWS is free; data transfer out to the internet is charged
Data transfer within the same region is always charged at standard rates
Data transfer between AZs in the same region is free

explanation.correct: A fundamental AWS pricing rule: data coming IN to AWS (from the internet) is always free. Data going OUT from AWS to the internet is charged. Cross-region and cross-AZ transfers have their own pricing but follow different rules.
explanation.why: Cross-region transfers are typically charged. Intra-AZ transfer is usually free. Inter-AZ transfer has a small charge. The key exam fact is ingress free, egress charged.

questions.question: A company decides to use Amazon EC2 for their database server. After a major vulnerability is discovered in MySQL, the security team asks who needs to patch it. What is the CORRECT answer?

options.text: AWS — they manage all database software on AWS
The customer — EC2 is IaaS, and the customer manages all software they install
AWS — RDS handles all database patching
Shared — AWS patches the engine, customer patches the config files

explanation.correct: MySQL on EC2 is customer-managed. EC2 is IaaS — the customer chose to install MySQL themselves and is fully responsible for it. This contrasts with Amazon RDS (managed service) where AWS handles engine patching.
explanation.why: AWS manages MySQL patching ONLY in Amazon RDS. On EC2, the customer owns all software above the hypervisor. This distinction is critical and frequently tested.

questions.question: How many countries do AWS Points of Presence (Edge Locations) span?

options.text: 10+ countries
25+ countries
40+ countries
100+ countries

explanation.correct: AWS has 400+ Points of Presence across 90+ cities in 40+ countries.
explanation.why: 40+ is the correct number from AWS documentation. 100+ would be incorrect — AWS has many locations but not in 100+ countries.

questions.question: What analogy BEST describes the relationship between IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS?

options.text: IaaS = hotel room; PaaS = furnished apartment; SaaS = buying land
IaaS = buying land and building; PaaS = furnished apartment; SaaS = staying in a hotel
IaaS = SaaS with extra steps; PaaS = IaaS for developers
All three are equivalent but target different company sizes

explanation.correct: IaaS = buying a land plot (you build everything). PaaS = furnished apartment (structure provided, you furnish the rest). SaaS = hotel (everything is done for you, just use it). Each level removes more management responsibility.
explanation.why: The levels of abstraction increase from IaaS to SaaS. The hotel analogy correctly represents SaaS — nothing to manage. Buying land correctly represents IaaS — maximum flexibility, maximum responsibility.

questions.question: A company's application is currently only available to users in North America with high latency for users in Asia. They want to expand globally with low latency in 3 days. Which cloud advantage makes this possible?

options.text: Trade CAPEX for OPEX
Stop guessing capacity
Go global in minutes
Economies of scale

explanation.correct: AWS's global infrastructure of Regions worldwide enables teams to deploy in new geographic regions in minutes — not months. A team of 5 could deploy a global application leveraging existing AWS infrastructure.
explanation.why: CAPEX/OPEX is about financial model. Capacity guessing is about scaling. Economies of scale is about pricing. Geographic expansion = Go global in minutes.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a company using the cloud WITHOUT knowing it?

options.text: A developer using AWS EC2 directly
A DevOps team configuring AWS IAM roles
An individual using Netflix to stream a movie (Netflix runs on AWS)
A company using AWS CloudFormation to deploy infrastructure

explanation.correct: Netflix is an example of cloud usage that end users don't realize — they just watch movies. Netflix itself is built on AWS, but the viewer has no AWS account and is unaware they're using AWS infrastructure.
explanation.why: EC2, IAM, and CloudFormation users are explicitly using AWS — they know they're using the cloud. Netflix viewers are passively consuming a cloud-powered service without direct cloud awareness.

questions.question: An AWS Region has its services linked to that specific region. What happens if you create an EC2 instance in eu-west-1 (Ireland) and then switch your console to us-east-1 (N. Virginia)?

options.text: The EC2 instance is automatically replicated to us-east-1
You will not see the EC2 instance in us-east-1 — it only exists in eu-west-1
The instance moves to us-east-1 when you switch regions
Global services like EC2 are visible in all regions

explanation.correct: EC2 is a regional service. An instance created in eu-west-1 only exists in eu-west-1. Switching your console region to us-east-1 will not show resources from other regions — each region is completely separate.
explanation.why: AWS does not automatically replicate or move regional resources. EC2 is not a global service. This is the most common source of confusion for beginners.

questions.question: What does 'on-demand self-service' mean in cloud computing?

options.text: AWS representatives provision resources for you upon request
You can provision resources automatically without requiring human intervention from the cloud provider
You must call AWS support to get additional compute capacity
Self-service is only available for storage, not compute

explanation.correct: On-demand self-service means you can provision compute, storage, and other resources on your own through a web console or API without AWS employees being involved. You are in full control of what you create and when.
explanation.why: The whole point of on-demand self-service is eliminating the need to call or wait for the provider. You launch EC2 instances in seconds without AWS intervention.

questions.question: A company is migrating from on-premises to AWS. Their CTO asks: 'What do we stop worrying about after migration?' Which of the following can they STOP managing after migration to AWS managed services?

options.text: What data they store and who can access it
Physical server hardware replacement and maintenance
IAM user permissions and access policies
Encryption keys for their sensitive data

explanation.correct: Physical hardware maintenance, replacement, and failure management are AWS's responsibility. The customer never touches physical servers in AWS — this is one of the core benefits of cloud migration.
explanation.why: Data governance, IAM permissions, and encryption keys remain the customer's responsibility regardless of migration. These are 'security IN the cloud' responsibilities that never transfer to AWS.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the AWS Shared Responsibility Model is TRUE?

options.text: AWS is responsible for security of all data stored in S3 buckets
The responsibility boundary is the same for all AWS service types
The customer's responsibility increases when using IaaS compared to managed services
AWS manages IAM user password policies for customers

explanation.correct: With IaaS (EC2), the customer manages OS, runtime, applications, and security configuration. With managed services (RDS, Beanstalk), AWS takes over OS and infrastructure management. So the customer has MORE responsibility with IaaS than with PaaS/SaaS.
explanation.why: S3 data security is the customer's responsibility. The responsibility boundary shifts by service type. AWS never manages customer-specific IAM policies.

questions.question: An enterprise is using Amazon EC2 for all their workloads. To reduce operational overhead, they want to move their database workload to a managed service where they don't have to patch the database engine. Which service should they migrate to?

options.text: Amazon EC2 with a larger instance type
Amazon RDS
Amazon S3
AWS Lambda

explanation.correct: Amazon RDS (Relational Database Service) is a managed database PaaS service. AWS handles OS patching, database engine updates, backups, and multi-AZ failover. The customer only manages data, queries, and access control.
explanation.why: Larger EC2 instance doesn't remove patching responsibility. S3 is object storage, not a database. Lambda is for serverless compute, not traditional relational databases.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes the concept of 'measured service' in cloud computing?

options.text: AWS measures latency between regions
Resource usage is monitored and customers pay exactly for what they consume
AWS measures network packet loss to ensure reliability
Customers measure their own usage and report it to AWS for billing

explanation.correct: Measured service means cloud resource usage is metered and reported, and customers are billed only for what they consume. This is the technical foundation of pay-as-you-go pricing.
explanation.why: Latency and packet loss measurement are operational metrics, not billing-related cloud characteristics. Customers don't self-report usage — AWS automatically measures and bills it.

questions.question: Route 53 is listed as a Global Service in AWS. What does this mean practically for a DevOps engineer?

options.text: Route 53 can only be used with resources in the us-east-1 region
Route 53 configuration is the same regardless of which AWS region the engineer's console is set to
Route 53 automatically deploys to all regions simultaneously
Route 53 is managed by AWS and the customer has no configuration control

explanation.correct: Global services like Route 53 don't require a region selection. The DNS configuration you create is the same whether you access the console from any region — there's no 'Ireland version' or 'Virginia version' of your Route 53 hosted zones.
explanation.why: Global services work globally, not just us-east-1. They don't automatically deploy resources to all regions. Customers still configure global services — they're just not scoped to a region.

questions.question: Which component would you use to send network traffic from the internet to the correct device within a local network after it has already been routed to the right building?

options.text: Router
DNS Server
Switch
Firewall

explanation.correct: A switch operates at the local network level. Once a router has delivered traffic to the right network, the switch directs it to the specific device (server) within that network.
explanation.why: A router works between networks, not within them. DNS translates domain names to IP addresses. A firewall filters traffic based on rules.

questions.question: What were the two main services that AWS expanded with when it relaunched its public offering in 2006?

options.text: EC2 and Lambda
S3 and EC2 (alongside existing SQS)
RDS and VPC
IAM and CloudFront

explanation.correct: In 2006, AWS relaunched its offering by adding S3 (Simple Storage Service) and EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud) alongside the existing SQS — forming the foundational services of modern AWS.
explanation.why: Lambda, RDS, VPC, IAM, and CloudFront all came later in AWS's history.

questions.question: A retail company runs a Black Friday sale every year where traffic increases 20x for 8 hours. For the rest of the year, they run at baseline capacity. In traditional IT, they must buy 20x servers and let 19x sit idle for 357 days. Which cloud advantage DIRECTLY solves this?

options.text: Go global in minutes — deploy in new regions
Stop spending money on data centers
Stop guessing capacity — scale elastically based on demand
Trade CAPEX for OPEX — reduce upfront server costs

explanation.correct: The core problem is buying 20x capacity for 8 hours of peak demand and wasting the rest. Elastic scaling on AWS means running at baseline capacity year-round and scaling to 20x only during the 8-hour sale window — paying only for what's used.
explanation.why: While CAPEX→OPEX is also relevant, the specific technical solution is elastic capacity. 'Stop guessing capacity' covers both buying too much (waste) and buying too little (unavailability).

questions.question: In the AWS Acceptable Use Policy, which of the following is PROHIBITED?

options.text: Hosting a high-traffic e-commerce website
Running automated data processing jobs
Using AWS infrastructure to conduct unauthorized port scanning
Storing encrypted backups of production databases

explanation.correct: Unauthorized port scanning is a security violation explicitly prohibited by the AWS Acceptable Use Policy. This also includes DDoS attacks, hacking, and network abuse.
explanation.why: E-commerce hosting, automated processing, and encrypted backups are all legitimate, permitted uses of AWS.

questions.question: A company wants to use the cloud but their CEO worries about losing control of their hardware. Which deployment model gives them the benefits of cloud management while maintaining complete control over a single-organization environment?

options.text: Public Cloud
Multi-Cloud
Hybrid Cloud
Private Cloud

explanation.correct: A Private Cloud is a cloud environment used exclusively by one organization, not shared with the public. It can be managed internally or by a third party (like Rackspace), providing cloud management benefits with complete organizational control.
explanation.why: Public cloud is shared. Multi-cloud uses multiple public providers. Hybrid mixes on-premises and public cloud. Private cloud is the single-organization cloud model.

questions.question: An application team says they need to deploy to production in 2 hours to meet a deadline. Previously, this took 3 weeks because they had to order, rack, and configure physical servers. Which cloud advantage did they realize?

options.text: Economies of scale — servers cost less now
Increased speed and agility — infrastructure is available in minutes
Stop guessing capacity — no more over-provisioning
Measured service — they pay only 2 hours of compute

explanation.correct: The ability to provision servers in minutes (instead of weeks of hardware procurement) is the 'increased speed and agility' advantage. Teams can develop, test, and deploy faster because infrastructure barriers are eliminated.
explanation.why: Economies of scale is about pricing. Capacity guessing is about matching resources to demand. Measured service is about billing. The time reduction from 3 weeks to 2 hours = speed and agility.

questions.question: Which of the following CORRECTLY describes multi-tenancy in AWS?

options.text: Each AWS customer gets their own dedicated physical server
Multiple customers share the same physical infrastructure but are logically isolated from each other
AWS tenants are large enterprise customers only
Multi-tenancy means customers share the same AWS account

explanation.correct: Multi-tenancy means multiple customers (tenants) share the same underlying physical infrastructure. They are logically isolated at the hypervisor level — one customer cannot access another's data or resources.
explanation.why: Dedicated physical servers are available (Dedicated Hosts) but are not the default — shared is. Tenants are not limited to enterprises. Customers always have separate accounts.

questions.question: What is the PRIMARY purpose of Availability Zones being physically separated from each other within a region?

options.text: To reduce networking costs between data centers
To ensure disasters affecting one AZ do not cascade to other AZs
To allow AWS to service different customer types in each AZ
To provide different pricing tiers based on AZ selection

explanation.correct: AZs are intentionally physically separated so that natural disasters, power outages, or connectivity failures in one AZ don't impact others. This physical separation, combined with high-bandwidth interconnection, is what makes multi-AZ architectures highly available.
explanation.why: Cost reduction is a side effect, not the purpose. AZs serve the same customer types. AZ selection does not change pricing within a region.

questions.question: A SaaS company builds an application using Amazon EC2 for compute, Amazon S3 for storage, and calls Amazon Rekognition's API for image analysis. Which service model does Amazon Rekognition represent FROM THE COMPANY'S PERSPECTIVE?

options.text: IaaS — they're accessing raw infrastructure
PaaS — they're deploying on a managed platform
SaaS — they consume a complete ML service without managing models or infrastructure
On-premises — they control the ML models

explanation.correct: From the company's perspective, Rekognition is SaaS — they send an API call and receive image analysis results. They don't manage models, training data, infrastructure, or any underlying technology. It's a complete managed service consumed as-is.
explanation.why: IaaS would require managing compute. PaaS would require building models on a platform. SaaS is the consumption of a ready-made service — Rekognition fits this exactly.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of Availability Zones that an AWS Region can have?

explanation.correct: AWS Regions have a minimum of 3 and a maximum of 6 Availability Zones. Most regions have exactly 3 AZs.
explanation.why: 3 is the minimum. 10 would be excessive and is incorrect. 6 is the documented maximum.

questions.question: Which of the following is a GLOBAL AWS service that does NOT require region selection?

options.text: Amazon EC2
Amazon S3 (console)
AWS Lambda
Amazon Route 53

explanation.correct: Amazon Route 53 (DNS service) is a global service — when you open it in the console, it shows 'Global' in the region selector and your configuration applies worldwide.
explanation.why: EC2, Lambda, and S3 are all regional (despite S3's global namespace, buckets are created in specific regions). Route 53 is global by design.

questions.question: A company migrates their application to AWS and uses Amazon RDS instead of MySQL on EC2. Which of the following responsibilities does AWS NOW take over that the customer handled previously?

options.text: Deciding what data to store in the database
Creating database user accounts and permissions
Patching the database engine and underlying OS
Configuring application connection strings

explanation.correct: When migrating from MySQL on EC2 to Amazon RDS, the key shift is that AWS now handles database engine patching and OS patching. These were customer responsibilities on EC2, but RDS is a managed service where AWS owns the infrastructure layer.
explanation.why: Data decisions, database users, permissions, and application configurations remain the customer's responsibility even with RDS.

questions.question: Which of the following scenarios represents 'broad network access' as a cloud characteristic?

options.text: An AWS region having multiple Availability Zones
An employee accessing their company's AWS-hosted application from a smartphone in a coffee shop
AWS automatically scaling EC2 instances during peak load
Multiple customers sharing the same physical server

explanation.correct: Broad network access means cloud resources are available over the network and accessible through standard mechanisms (like browsers and apps) from any device — laptops, tablets, smartphones. The coffee shop scenario perfectly illustrates this.
explanation.why: Multiple AZs represent fault isolation. Auto-scaling represents rapid elasticity. Shared physical servers represent resource pooling.

questions.question: A company is comparing traditional IT to cloud computing. In traditional IT, they spent $2M building a data center. This type of spending is called what?

options.text: OPEX — operational expenditure
CAPEX — capital expenditure
TCO — total cost of ownership
ROI — return on investment

explanation.correct: Building or buying physical infrastructure (data center, servers) is CAPEX — capital expenditure. You own the asset. Cloud computing shifts this to OPEX (paying for usage), which is one of the six cloud advantages.
explanation.why: OPEX is the ongoing usage-based model cloud uses. TCO is a metric that includes all costs over time. ROI measures the return relative to investment.

questions.question: A startup claims they will save money by managing their own servers instead of paying AWS. Under what condition would this claim be MOST valid?

options.text: If they have highly variable workloads with unpredictable spikes
If they have steady, predictable workloads running 24/7 at near-full capacity with a large engineering team
If they need to go global quickly with users worldwide
If they want to innovate and release features faster

explanation.correct: On-premises becomes cost-competitive when: workloads are steady and predictable (no need for elasticity), running near 100% capacity (no wasted resource), at very large scale (economies of hardware purchasing), with existing engineering teams. These conditions reduce the cloud's variable-cost advantage.
explanation.why: Variable and unpredictable workloads favor cloud (elastic scaling). Global deployment and agility always favor cloud. At steady high utilization, hardware ownership can sometimes beat pay-per-use pricing.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes why Netflix is used as an example in cloud computing courses?

options.text: Netflix invented cloud computing
Netflix is a major example of a large SaaS application built entirely on AWS
Netflix created the concept of pay-as-you-go
Netflix is an AWS competitor in the streaming space

explanation.correct: Netflix is one of the most prominent examples of a company that migrated entirely to AWS and uses AWS infrastructure at massive scale to deliver its video streaming SaaS service globally.
explanation.why: AWS (Amazon) invented modern public cloud. Netflix uses existing cloud concepts, not invented them. Netflix and AWS are partners, not competitors.

questions.question: A company is asked to choose a region for their new application. They have no compliance requirements, their users are split evenly between Europe and Asia, and they want the cheapest option. Which factor should GUIDE their decision most?

options.text: Compliance — always the first factor
Latency — deploy in the region closest to most users
Pricing — cheapest region wins with no compliance requirement
Service availability — check what services are available

explanation.correct: Without compliance requirements, user experience (latency) drives the decision. With users split between Europe and Asia, they should consider deploying in both regions (multi-region) or in a geographically central region. Pricing is secondary to user experience.
explanation.why: Compliance doesn't apply here. Price is a tiebreaker, not the primary driver when user experience is affected. Service availability matters but assumes they've identified the services they need.

questions.question: Which statement CORRECTLY describes how a Switch differs from a Router in networking?

options.text: A switch works between networks; a router works within a network
A router works between networks directing traffic; a switch delivers traffic to specific devices within a local network
A switch assigns IP addresses; a router encrypts traffic
Routers and switches are the same device with different names

explanation.correct: Routers work between networks — they direct internet traffic from source to destination across multiple networks. Switches work within a local network — once traffic arrives at the right location, the switch delivers it to the specific correct device.
explanation.why: The router-switch distinction is about scope: inter-network (router) vs intra-network (switch). They are distinct devices with distinct functions.

questions.question: Which of the following CORRECTLY describes what 'on-demand delivery' means in the context of cloud computing?

options.text: AWS delivers physical servers to your location within 24 hours
Resources are available immediately when requested without advance notice or advance ordering
You must order resources 30 days in advance to guarantee availability
AWS delivers services only during business hours

explanation.correct: On-demand delivery means resources are provisioned instantly, on request. You need a server? You have it in seconds. No purchase orders, no lead time, no advance notice required.
explanation.why: Physical delivery is the old model. Advance ordering is what cloud eliminates. AWS services are available 24/7 globally.

questions.question: A company has a data processing job that runs for 6 hours every Sunday night and requires 100 EC2 instances. For the rest of the week, no compute is needed. What is the MOST cost-effective approach on AWS?

options.text: Buy 100 Reserved Instances to ensure availability every Sunday
Run 100 EC2 instances 24/7 to always be ready
Launch 100 instances before the Sunday job, run the job, then terminate them — paying only for 6 hours per week
Use 1 very large instance to replace 100 smaller instances

explanation.correct: This is the cloud economic model at its best — launch when needed, terminate when done, pay only for 6 hours per week. On-premises or always-on cloud would charge for 168 hours/week. Pay-as-you-go makes this workload dramatically cheaper.
explanation.why: Reserved instances commit you to 1-year or 3-year terms — wasteful for a 6-hour weekly job. 24/7 instances are unnecessary and costly. One large instance cannot simply replace 100 parallel processors.

questions.question: What was the FIRST public AWS service, launched in 2004?

options.text: Amazon EC2
Amazon S3
Amazon SQS
Amazon RDS

explanation.correct: Amazon SQS (Simple Queue Service) was the first AWS service offered publicly, in 2004. EC2 and S3 followed in 2006 when AWS relaunched its public offering.
explanation.why: EC2 and S3 launched together in 2006, not 2004. RDS came much later. SQS was the pioneering public AWS service.

questions.question: Under the Shared Responsibility Model, a customer enables Amazon S3 Server-Side Encryption. Who is responsible for ensuring encryption is properly configured?

options.text: AWS — they automatically enforce encryption on all S3 data
The customer — enabling and configuring encryption is their choice and responsibility
Shared equally — AWS provides the encryption capability, customer turns it on
Neither — encryption is optional and has no responsibility owner

explanation.correct: AWS provides the encryption capability and the underlying key management infrastructure. However, deciding to enable encryption, selecting the key type, and configuring bucket policies are the customer's responsibility. AWS doesn't enforce encryption unless the customer requires it.
explanation.why: AWS does not automatically encrypt all data — that's the customer's choice. The 'shared' framing is misleading here; configuring encryption settings is clearly the customer's domain.

questions.question: A cloud architect is designing a highly available system. They decide to deploy application servers across 3 Availability Zones. One AZ suffers a complete power outage. What happens to the application?

options.text: The entire application goes down until the AZ is restored
The application continues to run from the other 2 AZs — users may see brief disruption as traffic reroutes
The application automatically migrates to a different region
AWS automatically provisions new instances in the failed AZ within seconds

explanation.correct: Multi-AZ deployment provides fault isolation. When one AZ fails, traffic is routed to the remaining healthy AZs. The application continues serving requests, though there may be a brief disruption as the load balancer detects the failure and reroutes traffic.
explanation.why: Single-AZ deployment would fail. AWS doesn't auto-migrate to different regions. AWS doesn't automatically provision in a failed AZ — that AZ is unavailable until restored.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST explains why AWS prices have generally decreased over time, benefiting all customers?

options.text: AWS reduces prices to stay competitive with Azure and Google Cloud
As more customers use AWS, AWS can negotiate better hardware deals and operate more efficiently, passing savings on
AWS prices decrease because cloud technology becomes obsolete quickly
AWS pricing decreases are tied to cryptocurrency market performance

explanation.correct: Economies of scale: as AWS grows, they purchase more hardware at better prices, build more efficient data centers, and optimize operations. These cost reductions are passed to customers as price decreases — a direct benefit of the shared, large-scale cloud model.
explanation.why: Competition may accelerate price drops but isn't the primary mechanism. Technology obsolescence affects hardware costs but indirectly. Cryptocurrency has no relation to AWS pricing.

questions.question: A company using AWS wants to understand what 'security IN the cloud' means under the Shared Responsibility Model. Which of the following is the MOST comprehensive description?

options.text: AWS's responsibility for securing the physical infrastructure
The customer's responsibility for their data, access controls, OS configuration, application security, and network settings within their AWS environment
AWS's responsibility for preventing DDoS attacks on customer applications
The customer's responsibility only for encrypting data at rest

explanation.correct: Security IN the cloud encompasses the customer's full scope: protecting their data (at rest and in transit), managing who has access (IAM), configuring OS-level security (EC2), securing their applications, and configuring network controls (security groups, NACLs). It is comprehensive, not limited to one aspect.
explanation.why: Security OF the cloud (physical infrastructure) is AWS's domain. DDoS protection infrastructure is AWS's responsibility (AWS Shield), though customer-level DDoS rules (WAF) are the customer's. 'Only encrypting data' dramatically understates customer security responsibilities.
